targets.authors: Steinberg S, Stefansson H, Jonsson T, Johannsdottir H, Ingason A, Helgason H
targets.title: Loss-of-function variants in ABCA7 confer risk of Alzheimer's disease
targets.evidence_quote: In the original study, Steinberg et al. [ 1 ] genotyped the ABCA7 variants on 6681 European non-Icelandic individuals and only four variants were polymorphic (Supplementary Table 5 from Steinberg et al. [ 1 ]). Therefore, we decided to genotype the variants that were found to be polymorphic on the non-Icelandic population together with the GWAS common variant.
targets.outcome_quote: Despite these limitations, we were able to replicate the original report.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The explicit overall verdict confirms the original report. Failure of individual rare variants is acknowledged but does not override that whole-report verdict.

targets.authors: Lambert JC, Ibrahim-Verbaas CA, Harold D, Naj AC, Sims R, Bellenguez C, et al.
targets.title: Meta-analysis of 74,046 individuals identifies 11 new susceptibility loci for Alzheimer's disease.
targets.evidence_quote: The ABCA7 GWAS common variant (rs4147929) as well as the loss-of-function variants (p.Glu709Alafs*86, p.Leu1403Argfs*7, rs200538373, and rs113809142) reported by Steinberg et al. [ 1 ] were genotyped in our dataset using competitive allele-specific polymerase chain reaction KASPar genotyping technologies as described previously [ 3 , 4 ].
targets.outcome_quote: In our dataset, the common variant rs4147929[A] was significantly associated with AD risk (Table 1 ; OR = 1.162, P = 0.022), suggesting that we have enough power to replicate known associations for common variants.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The GWAS ABCA7 common-variant association is deliberately genotyped and independently replicated; citation 2 identifies the publication that reported that signal.

reasoning: New European-American subjects retest Steinberg’s rare-variant finding and the independently published GWAS common-variant signal cited to Lambert. Other disease genes and rare-variant studies are methodological/background discussion. Steinberg receives successful under the authors’ explicit overall replication verdict despite individual rare-variant failures.
